what_this_is: The correctness anchor for this package. Build the runtime in tools/llama2c/ (see tools/llama2c/BUILD-AND-RUN.md), run each `argv` below from the extracted package root, take stdout, replace CRLF with LF, and compare against `stdout_text` or hash it against `stdout_sha256_lf`. A match means the container, the weights layout, the tokenizer layout and the whole forward pass are all right. Nothing weaker proves that: a runtime that reads the weights at the wrong offsets still emits confident text.
how_to_verify: 1. Build: see tools/llama2c/BUILD-AND-RUN.md section 2. There is no prebuilt binary in this package and nothing here is executed for you.
2. Run vectors[i].argv with your binary in place of '<the binary you built>'. The generated text is on stdout; the 'achieved tok/s' line is on stderr and is not part of any vector.

3. Normalise: replace CRLF with LF. run.c writes to a text-mode stream, so an identical computation emits \n on POSIX and \r\n through a Windows console. The hash is declared over the LF form; stdout_sha256_crlf records the raw Windows form of the same bytes so the normalisation itself is checkable.
4. Compare against stdout_sha256_lf. That is the whole check.
on_mismatch: A mismatch is diagnostic, not merely a failure, and the three cases are distinguishable. (a) FLUENT ENGLISH, DIVERGING AFTER N TOKENS: floating-point reassociation. The forward pass is scalar C but a vectorising compiler may reassociate the reductions in rmsnorm, softmax and matmul, and -ffast-math will. Report N and your flags; this is an arithmetic difference, not a broken reader. (b) FLUENT ENGLISH, DIFFERENT FROM TOKEN 1: the prompt encoding differs - check the BOS token and the SentencePiece dummy-prefix space, spec/layouts/llama2c-tokenizer.layout.txt section 5. (c) GARBAGE FROM TOKEN 1: the weights are being read at the wrong offsets - check the two DEAD RoPE tables, spec/layouts/llama2c-checkpoint.layout.txt section 4.
token_ids_note: token_ids is the stronger anchor because integers have no newline convention. THE UNMODIFIED run.c DOES NOT PRINT THEM: they were captured by a two-line instrumentation, which travels beside this file as tokens_instrumentation.diff, a unified diff against this package's own tools/llama2c/run.c. Apply it, rebuild, and stderr carries one 'TOKEN <id>' line per step. The first id is always 1 (BOS). Matching stdout_sha256_lf needs no patching and is sufficient.
